originalTitle: Treasury yields are lower after reaching multiyear highs, traders weigh latest bond auction
summary: Traders digested comments from a top Federal Reserve official while awaiting another long-dated bond auction.
content:
The yield on the 10-year Treasury fell on Thursday as traders digested comments from a top Federal Reserve official along with another long-dated bond auction.

The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield was down more than 4 basis points at 5.229% after reaching its highest level since 2002 this week. The 30-year Treasury bond yield dropped more than 5 basis points to 5.602% after trading around a 24-year high recently.

One basis point is equal to 0.01%, and yields and prices move in opposite directions.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller said on Thursday that more hikes are needed to bring inflation down after around 5-and-a-half years above the central bank's 2% target, but suggested rates did not need to rise immediately.

"The hikes do not need to come at consecutive meetings," Waller told a Central Bank of Turkey forum in Istanbul. "But they should be in place in an acceptable period of time."

His comments initially sent yields higher on the day. However, rates gave back those advances after President Donald Trump said the U.S. won't attack Iran until after the November midterm election . Yields also pulled back after a solid 30-year Treasury bond auction.

The department sold $22 billion in 30-year paper, with indirect bidders — which include central banks — scooping up 72.3% of the sale. That's above a 10-auction average of 68%. Direct bidders, including institutional investors, took 20.9% of the auction, just below an average of 22%. The yield at auction ease 5.618%.

That marks the final auction of the week. The department sold $58 billion in 3-year notes on Tuesday and another $39 billion in 10-year notes.

Thursday's sale "was decent but nowhere close to as good as the 10 yr auction yesterday," wrote Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer of One Point BFG Wealth Partners.

— CNBC's Brianna Bernath contributed reporting.
chineseTitle: 美国国债收益率在达到多年高位后走低，交易员权衡最新的债券拍卖
chineseSummary: 交易员在等待另一次长期债券拍卖时消化了美联储高级官员的评论。
chineseContent:
由于交易员消化了美联储高级官员的评论以及另一场长期债券拍卖，十年期国债收益率周四下跌。

基准10年期国债收益率本周触及2002年以来的最高水平，下跌超过4个基点至5.229%。 30年期国债收益率近期触及24年高点附近，下跌逾5个基点至5.602%。

1个基点等于0.01%，收益率和价格走势相反。

美联储理事克里斯托弗·沃勒(Christopher Waller)周四表示，在高于央行2%目标约五年半后，需要进一步加息才能降低通胀率，但暗示利率不需要立即加息。

沃勒在伊斯坦布尔举行的土耳其央行论坛上表示：“加息不需要在连续会议上进行。” “但它们应该在可接受的时间内就位。”

他的言论最初推高了当天的收益率。然而，在唐纳德·特朗普总统表示美国在 11 月中期选举之后才会攻击伊朗后，利率回吐了这些涨幅。在30年期国债拍卖强劲之后，收益率也有所回落。

该部门出售了价值 220 亿美元的 30 年期票据，其中包括央行在内的间接竞标者获得了 72.3% 的销售额。这高于 10 次拍卖的平均 68%。包括机构投资者在内的直接竞标者获得了 20.9% 的拍卖份额，略低于 22% 的平均水平。拍卖收益率为5.618%。

这标志着本周的最后一次拍卖。该部门周二出售了 580 亿美元的 3 年期票据，并另外出售了 390 亿美元的 10 年期票据。

One Point BFG Wealth Partners 首席投资官 Peter Boockvar 写道，周四的拍卖“不错，但远不及昨天的 10 年期拍卖”。

— CNBC 的 Brianna Bernath 贡献了报道。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
